grades.quote: Preemptive multitasking does not need any fundamentally different thread switching mechanism; it simply needs the addition of a hardware interrupt mechanism.
grades.reason: Provides background on interrupt-driven preemption, but does not explain why disabling local interrupts leaves other CPUs unaffected.
Discusses supervisor facilities and virtualization, not synchronization or the limits of disabling local interrupts.

grades.quote: One line of reasoning is that this should be allowed: no other CPU can hold the lock, so there’s no need to worry about CPUs interfering with each others’ use of the protected data.
grades.reason: Explains the role of locks in preventing interference between CPUs, but does not address interrupt disabling.

grades.quote: Yielding while holding a lock would also violate the requirement that interrupts must be off while a spinlock is held.
